sections.h2: Where is Stillwater, Oklahoma, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Stillwater is a college city in north-central Oklahoma, about 60 miles north-northeast of downtown Oklahoma City and 63 miles west of downtown Tulsa by road. It covers 28.3 square miles, almost all of it land, according to Census figures repeated by Wikipedia.

Two highways cross the city. State Highway 51, also called 6th Avenue, runs east and west, and U.S. 177, known locally as Perkins Road, runs north and south. A 7.2-mile spur links U.S. 177 to the Cimarron Turnpike.

Stillwater Regional Airport has served the city since 1917, and American Airlines began flights to Dallas/Fort Worth there in August 2016, flown by SkyWest. Public transit is run as OSU-Stillwater Community Transit, which Wikipedia says operates ten routes across the city and campus. These details are worth knowing if you are explaining the location to an out-of-town heir or investor who has never seen the house.

sections.h2: How much does Oklahoma State University shape the Stillwater housing market?
sections.html:
Heavily. Oklahoma State University's Institutional Research office reports 30,683 students enrolled for Fall 2026: 22,895 undergraduates, 6,694 graduate students, 1,082 professional students and 12 non-credit students. It also lists 1,819 faculty members as of Fall 2025.

Wikipedia, citing the Chamber of Commerce's list of existing industries, shows the biggest local employers as OSU (6,007), Stillwater Medical Center (1,031), OnCue Express (903), Stillwater Public Schools (779) and the City of Stillwater (585). The page does not date those counts, so treat them as a rough ranking rather than current headcounts.

For a seller, the university means a large student and employee population sits behind local housing demand, so a student-oriented rental is a different kind of asset from a family home. If you own from out of town, such as a parent or an heir, a house with tenants or deferred repairs can be easier to sell as-is than to renovate from a distance.

sections.h2: What are Stillwater's short-term rental rules?
sections.html:
Stillwater requires a license for any short-term rental. Ordinance No. 3604 sets the rules, and the city's page confirms that all short-term rentals must be licensed.

ItemWhat the city says
LicenseAnnual license required to manage or operate a short-term rental
Density capNo more than 20 percent of a residential block
ApplicationProof of ownership and state tax compliance
TransferLicenses are non-transferable, per the ordinance text
Fees in the ordinance$100 initial, $10 renewal

The non-transferable license matters if you bought a house with a license in place. A new owner cannot simply take it over. A buyer who plans to run the house as a rental has to apply on their own and must fit under the block's density cap. Applications filed after a renewal deadline must also meet the cap.

The city publishes a list of active licenses, which is a quick way to see whether your block is crowded. Development Services at 405-742-8220 answers questions. If you are selling a house that was an unlicensed short-term rental, bring that up with a local attorney before you list.

sections.h2: How does Stillwater handle code enforcement and property nuisances?
sections.html:
Code Enforcement in Stillwater is a division of the police department, and it issues citations for structural and non-structural problems. Dilapidated or unsecured structures can be reported with an online complaint form.

The city's nuisance page lists these items:

  • Grass, weeds or brush over 12 inches that create a health, safety or welfare problem
  • Broken windows, roof and gutter problems, missing siding and peeling paint
  • Inoperable or untagged vehicles and trailers
  • Dilapidated, open or vacant buildings, which may not stay boarded for more than 36 months
  • Trash carts with lids that do not close

If a problem stays unfixed, the city may hire a contractor to mow, board up, demolish or clear debris, bill the owner, and place a tax lien on the property to recover the cost. Judicial remedies can include fines of up to $549 per day per violation, depending on the violation. The city does not state fixed deadlines, saying each violation has its own time limit.

For a seller, an open nuisance case is a loose end. Resolve it or disclose it, because a lien tied to the property can surface during title work.

sections.h2: What weather risks should Stillwater sellers expect buyers to ask about?
sections.html:
Stillwater has a humid subtropical climate in Tornado Alley, with frequent spring tornado watches and warnings. Wikipedia reports that summer highs reach or pass 100 degrees about ten times a year, the average January high is 49.8 degrees, and average snowfall is 7.5 inches.

The record high is 115 degrees, set on August 11, 1936, and the record low is minus 21, recorded on February 10, 2011. That swing means heating and cooling systems, attic insulation and roof condition all come up in an inspection.

Payne County's assessor offers a storm shelter exemption for up to 100 square feet of an eligible tornado shelter or safe room added after January 1, 2002. If your house has one, keep the installation record and the exemption paperwork for the buyer.

sections.h2: Who serves Stillwater with schools and utilities?
sections.html:
Stillwater Public Schools covers almost all of the city, including every residential area, and enrolls more than 5,400 students. Its schools include Highland Park, Richmond, Sangre Ridge, Skyline, Westwood and Will Rogers elementaries, Stillwater Middle School, Stillwater Junior High, Stillwater High School and Lincoln Academy. A small piece of the city, occupied by airport property, is in Morrison Public Schools.

Utilities are unusual. Stillwater has had a community-owned electric utility since 1907, and the Stillwater Utilities Authority now provides electric, water, wastewater and solid waste service. Water comes from Kaw Lake and is pumped about 40 miles to the treatment plant. Ask the city how it handles a final reading and account transfer at closing.

sections.h2: How does property tax work for a Stillwater seller?
sections.html:
Payne County values and bills Stillwater properties. The Payne County Assessor is at 315 W. 6th Avenue, Suite 102, in Stillwater, and its number is 405-747-8300.

The Assessor's page lists these relief programs:

  • Homestead exemption: reduces the assessed value of an eligible primary residence by $1,000, generally if you own and occupy the home on January 1
  • Additional homestead: another $1,000 for qualifying homeowners with household income of $30,000 or less
  • Senior valuation limitation: caps increases in fair cash value for a head of household age 65 or older who meets the income limit, without freezing the bill
  • Disabled veteran and surviving spouse exemptions, and the storm shelter exemption

For disputes, the Oklahoma Tax Commission's informal protest form says a taxpayer has 30 calendar days from the date the valuation notice was mailed to file a written complaint with the assessor. Payne County also runs an online appeal system.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in Stillwater?
sections.html:
A listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale and a cash sale all work in Stillwater. Which fits depends on the house and how soon you need to be done.

A listing suits a house in good condition near campus when you can wait on showings and a buyer's loan. A cash sale suits a house with tenant wear, deferred repairs, a code notice, or an owner who lives far away. Before choosing, collect your deed, lease copies if any, utility account details and your latest tax statement. If the house was a short-term rental, add the license record.

faqs.a: Payne County. The Payne County Assessor in Stillwater handles valuation and exemptions, and the county treasurer bills the tax.

faqs.q: Can a buyer keep my Stillwater short-term rental license?
faqs.a: No. Ordinance No. 3604 makes licenses non-transferable, so the new owner has to apply and must fit under the 20 percent block density cap.

faqs.q: How big is Oklahoma State University?
faqs.a: OSU's Institutional Research office reports 30,683 students enrolled for Fall 2026, including 22,895 undergraduates and 6,694 graduate students.

faqs.q: What happens if I ignore a Stillwater code notice before selling?
faqs.a: The city may hire a contractor, bill you and place a tax lien on the property, and fines of up to $549 per day per violation are possible for some violations. Clear the case or disclose it before closing.

faqs.q: How long do I have to protest a Payne County valuation?
faqs.a: The Oklahoma Tax Commission's protest form gives 30 calendar days from the date the valuation notice was mailed to file with the county assessor. Call 405-747-8300 to confirm your dates.
